children: Amazon.com is raising the minimum starting wage for its U.S. full-time core operations employees to $20 an hour.
The e-commerce company announced the $1 per hour increase on Wednesday, alongside several new benefits like discounts on groceries.

Amazon said average pay for its U.S. core operations employees now reaches nearly $24 an hour, with average total compensation of more than $32 an hour including the value of its benefits package. The company said its minimum starting pay has increased more than 17% in the past three years.

The company also said it would give employees a new grocery discount, including 10% off on eligible groceries and other essentials on Amazon.com and Whole Foods Market online, as well as 20% off in-store at Whole Foods.
The discount will be available to every Amazon employee in the U.S. starting Oct. 1, the company said.

Amazon also said it's rolling out access to a new banking benefit, offering employees and their families a membership in First Tech Federal Credit Union that provides low-cost banking services they can keep for life.

Amazon said the offering-which includes $0 overdraft fees and no account minimums on standard checking and savings accounts, plus access to credit cards and loans-aims to help employees manage their money and plan for the future.
Access will begin rolling out in late 2026 and become broadly available in 2027, the company said.
